title: What If You Had a Chimpanzee's Muscles? Not 5 Times Stronger

scenes.text: What if you had a chimpanzee's muscles? You'd be stronger. Just not the way the internet says.
Since the 1920s people have claimed chimps are three, four, almost five times stronger than us, pound for pound.
In 2017 scientists measured chimp muscle fibers directly. The real number: about 1.35 times your force and power.
The fibers are almost identical to yours. Chimps just carry about twice as many fast-twitch fibers, built for sudden bursts.
So you'd jump higher and punch harder. Within minutes, though, you'd be gassed. Fast-twitch fibers tire quickly.
Your slow-twitch muscle is the trade. It let your ancestors walk and run for hours. A chimp can't follow you there.

description:
What if you had a chimpanzee's muscles? A 2017 study in PNAS measured chimp muscle fibers and found they produce about 1.35 times the force and power of human muscle, far below the old claims of 3 to 5 times.
The fibers are nearly identical; chimps simply have about twice as many fast-twitch fibers for bursts of power, while humans evolved more slow-twitch fibers for endurance and long-distance travel.
